retrieved_synopses: Danis is a frightened tiefling from the grove, currently imprisoned in Moonrise Towers and frantic about his partner Bex (who the player may have met earlier at the Last Light Inn). He recognizes the player as someone from the grove but, shaken by Zevlor’s betrayal, immediately suspects anyone of colluding with the Absolute and oscillates between panic, accusation, and pleading. Off‑screen the tower is on high alert after recent events and a zealous half‑orc jailer watches the cells, can probe for tadpoles, and will punish or report escape attempts, so the exchange happens under dangerous scrutiny. Other captured tieflings (Lia, Lakrissa, Cal, Rolan) and imprisoned gnomes led by Wulbren are part of an ongoing, fragile jailbreak plan; Danis can act as an alternate quest contact to free the prisoners if Lia and Lakrissa are no longer available. The player’s tone (threaten to leave, promise rescue, or berate him) will strongly affect Danis’s frantic reactions.

Danis' dialog in Haven after his rescue.He has made it safely to Haven after escaping Moonrise Towers and has been reunited with Bex, his partner, if she's alive, or is alone if she's not. If she's alive, the player witnessed a really cute reunion between them, and these dialogues cover Danis' followups to that conversation, as well as versions for if he's alone and for a few states in Haven. Not all states are covered since Danis doesn't care much about Ketheric

In these dialogues, Zevlor reflects on what's happened (an attack of goblins at the gate, which the player helped with) and his mistrust of and bitterness towards the druids who are reluctantly hosting his people. He is exasperated, furious, but also eager to meet anyone who could help. In the same dialogue, we can also uncover that he is in fact a traitor, concerned only with getting these people through the goblins so he can trade them for his own safety later. In truth he is resentful and contemptuous of them, viewing them as weak.

He is exasperated, furious, but also eager to meet anyone who could help. He'll show a flash of anger and frustration at the start if the player struck him, but is pragmatic enough to calm himself once he realises you could be more help to him than harm.

The player is likely trying to reassure her and promise rescue; if Lia is already dead Lakrissa abandons quips and delivers the main beats about the tiefling rescue. Finally, other captured tieflings (Cal, Lia, Rolan) and their fate are relevant background and may come up in dialogue.
